julian-assange.body_append:
## Kiriakou on the Eastern District case (2020)

On the *#FreeAssangeVigil* in May 2020, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said the greatest strategic risk in [Julian Assange](/wiki/julian-assange)'s prosecution was that neither the mainstream media nor Assange's defence had fully absorbed the peculiar terrain of the [Eastern District of Virginia](/wiki/eastern-district-of-virginia): the district's jury pool is drawn heavily from [CIA](/wiki/cia), Pentagon, DHS, [FBI](/wiki/fbi) and intelligence-contractor employees; Judge [Leonie Brinkema](/wiki/leonie-brinkema) had been passed over for the case in favour of a chief judge who was *"a FISA court judge before he was named to the Eastern District"*; and the courtroom would be run under SIPA classified-information procedures — plastic sheeting on the windows, code words substituted for classified terms — that Kiriakou argues bias juries towards conviction.<Cite t="36:16" /><Cite t="36:47" /><Cite t="37:18" /><Cite t="37:48" /><Cite t="38:19" /> Kiriakou said the only remaining defence-side lever was *"jury nullification"* — the one right-thinking juror out of twelve — and that he would personally support leafleting the Alexandria courthouse in the spirit of the Fully Informed Jury Association.<Cite t="41:58" /><Cite t="43:02" /><Cite t="43:32" />

## Under Obama, mainstream journalists as unindicted co-conspirators

Kiriakou notes the Assange case is only the endpoint of a longer trajectory. Under the [Barack Obama](/wiki/barack-obama) administration, he said, mainstream reporters were formally described by the Attorney General as *"unindicted co-conspirators"* and their homes raided — a precedent, in his framing, that leaves *"literally nothing to stop the government from targeting"* the [New York Times](/wiki/consortium-news) and the *Washington Post* next if Assange is convicted.<Cite t="23:19" /><Cite t="23:51" /><Cite t="24:22" />

leonie-brinkema.body_append:
## Passed over for the Assange case (2020)

On the *#FreeAssangeVigil* in May 2020, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said he had *"predicted for a long time — wrongly, as it turned out — that Julian's judge would be Judge [Leonie Brinkema](/wiki/leonie-brinkema),"* who *"usually reserves these national security cases for herself."* The case was, however, taken away from her by the chief judge of the [Eastern District of Virginia](/wiki/eastern-district-of-virginia), a jurist Kiriakou notes *"just happens to have been a FISA court judge before he was named to the Eastern District"* — an alignment that, he said, *"makes me want to run screaming from the room."*<Cite t="36:47" /><Cite t="37:18" />

espionage-act.body_append:
## Trial mechanics in the 'espionage court'

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has described the physical staging of an [Espionage Act](/wiki/espionage-act) trial in the [Eastern District of Virginia](/wiki/eastern-district-of-virginia) as designed to bias juries towards conviction. Under the Classified Information Procedures Act (SIPA), he said in 2020, the courtroom is closed to the public and press, its windows and doors are covered with *"plastic sheeting and duct tape so no one can aim a laser beam at the windows and pick up the vibrations,"* and the jury is issued a small paper substituting placeholder words for classified terms — *"NSA equals Zebra,"* and so on. Kiriakou argues that the substitution alone tells the jury that *"even these individual words are so highly classified that we can't even utter them in this closed courtroom — so he must be guilty."*<Cite t="37:18" /><Cite t="37:48" /><Cite t="38:19" /><Cite t="38:51" />

john-kiriakou.body_append:
## Taking the plea — the O.J. Simpson jury consultant

Ahead of his own [Espionage Act](/wiki/espionage-act) trial, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said on the *#FreeAssangeVigil* in May 2020, he hired the veteran jury consultant Robert Hirschhorn — the father of a friend's wife, who worked for him pro bono. Hirschhorn had also consulted on the trials of O.J. Simpson, William Kennedy Smith and George Zimmerman and, in Kiriakou's words, has *"literally never lost a case."* After Hirschhorn was cleared to review the 15,000 pages of discovery, he sat Kiriakou down and told him: *"If we were in any other district in America I would say let's go for it, we're going to win this thing. But the [Eastern District of Virginia](/wiki/eastern-district-of-virginia) — your jury is going to be made up of employees or family members of employees of the [CIA](/wiki/cia), the Pentagon, the Department of Homeland Security, the [FBI](/wiki/fbi), intelligence-community contractors. You don't have a chance. It's all stacked against you. That's why they charged you here in the first place. Take the deal."* Kiriakou took the deal.<Cite t="39:21" /><Cite t="39:53" /><Cite t="40:25" /><Cite t="40:56" />

## On the 2016 Gary Johnson tour and the absent benefactor

Kiriakou said he traveled to twelve states in 2016 with the Libertarian presidential nominee Gary Johnson, and that Johnson mentioned to him almost offhandedly a structural weakness of third-party politics that stuck with him: the Libertarian Party had *"no benefactor."* *"There was a family in California that made its money in canned tomatoes … that had been very generous, but in terms of an actual ongoing benefactor there just wasn't one — the [Democrats](/wiki/barack-obama) and the Republicans have hundreds of such benefactors."* Kiriakou extended the observation to independent journalism: *"we need a benefactor whether that media is on the left or the right, because it's one thing to write for these outlets — it's another thing for the news to actually get out there."*<Cite t="17:35" /><Cite t="18:06" /><Cite t="18:37" />

## News-consumption habits, 2020

Asked in May 2020 for a post-partisan path forward on civil liberties, Kiriakou said he had already stopped consuming mainstream media almost entirely: *"I for one get my news from the likes of [Consortium News](/wiki/consortium-news) and Reader Supported News and outlets like that. I scan outlets on the left and the right, and I've gotten to the point where I rarely go to the mainstream media — I think I'm not alone in that."*<Cite t="17:04" />
